pharm: Anthracycline topoisomerase II inhibitor that intercalates into DNA, inhibits nucleic acid and protein synthesis, triggers DNA cleavage, and generates cytotoxic free radicals.
quick: 100-120 mg/m2 IV per cycle (e.g., FEC-100 or CEF-120)
Can cause fetal harm; avoid in 1st trimester; use contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for >=7 days after last dose
Consider lower dose if serum creatinine >5 mg/dL
Reduce dose if bilirubin/AST elevated; contraindicated if severe
Not a primary concern; avoid hepatotoxins
LVEF, CBC, bilirubin/AST, creatinine, uric acid/electrolytes
summary: Epirubicin (Ellence) is an anthracycline cytotoxic agent given intravenously as a component of adjuvant therapy for node-positive breast cancer. It carries a BOXED WARNING for cumulative dose-related cardiomyopathy/CHF, secondary AML/MDS, severe local tissue necrosis on extravasation, and severe myelosuppression. It must be given by a physician experienced in cytotoxic therapy, with LVEF and blood count monitoring, dose reduction in hepatic impairment, and a cumulative dose generally limited to below 900 mg/m2.
indications: Component of adjuvant therapy in patients with evidence of axillary node tumor involvement following resection of primary breast cancer

dosage.t: Repeated 3- to 4-week cycles; total dose on Day 1 or divided Days 1 and 8
dosage.n: Infuse over 15-20 min into tubing of a freely running IV; 120 mg/m2 regimen requires prophylactic antibiotics

dosage.d: Epirubicin 100 mg/m2 IV Day 1, with 5-FU 500 mg/m2 and cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m2 Day 1
Epirubicin 60 mg/m2 IV Days 1 and 8, with cyclophosphamide 75 mg/m2 PO Days 1-14 and 5-FU 500 mg/m2 IV Days 1 and 8
dosage.n: Prophylactic antibiotics with 120 mg/m2 total dose
Bilirubin >3 mg/dL or AST >4x ULN; do NOT use if Child-Pugh C or bilirubin >5 mg/dL
For pre-existing marrow depression or neoplastic marrow infiltration

admin: Administer only by personnel experienced in cytotoxic chemotherapy; it is a hazardous, vesicant drug
Give IV into tubing of a freely flowing infusion (0.9% NaCl or 5% glucose) over 15-20 min at standard doses; never less than 3 minutes
Direct IV push is not recommended due to extravasation risk; avoid veins over joints or in compromised limbs
Do NOT mix with heparin or fluorouracil (precipitation) or alkaline solutions (hydrolysis); do not mix with other drugs in the same syringe
If extravasation suspected, stop immediately, apply ice 15 min 4x/day for 3 days, and consider dexrazoxane within 6 hours
Use within 24 hours of first stopper penetration / removal from refrigeration; discard unused portion
moa: Epirubicin is an anthracycline cytotoxic agent. It forms a complex with DNA by intercalating its planar rings between nucleotide base pairs, inhibiting DNA and RNA and protein synthesis. This intercalation triggers DNA cleavage by topoisomerase II, producing cytocidal activity. Epirubicin also inhibits DNA helicase, preventing strand separation and interfering with replication and transcription, and generates cytotoxic free radicals through oxidation-reduction reactions.

absolute: Recent myocardial infarction or severe arrhythmias
Previous treatment with maximum cumulative doses of anthracyclines
Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C or serum bilirubin >5 mg/dL)
Severe hypersensitivity to epirubicin, other anthracyclines, or anthracenediones
relative: Concomitant cardiotoxic agents (e.g., trastuzumab, calcium channel blockers)
monitor: Baseline and serial LVEF (echocardiogram or MUGA) and ECG
Complete blood counts before each cycle
Serum total bilirubin, AST, and creatinine before and during therapy
Uric acid, potassium, calcium, phosphate after initial treatment

preg: Can cause fetal harm based on animal data and mechanism of action; avoid use during the 1st trimester. Human data do not establish presence or absence of major birth defects/miscarriage with 2nd/3rd trimester use, and rare reports of fetal/neonatal cardiotoxicity exist. Animals showed embryo-fetal lethality and structural malformations below the human dose. Advise effective contraception: females during and 6 months after the last dose; males with female partners of reproductive potential during and 3 months after; males with pregnant partners should use condoms during and at least 7 days after.
lact: No data on epirubicin in human milk; it is present in rat milk and likely passes into human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, advise lactating women not to breastfeed during treatment and for at least 7 days after the last dose.
renal: No significant pharmacokinetic alterations with serum creatinine <5 mg/dL. A ~50% reduction in clearance was reported with serum creatinine >5 mg/dL; consider lower doses in severe renal impairment. Patients on dialysis have not been studied.
hepatic: Epirubicin is eliminated mainly hepatobiliarily; clearance falls with hepatic dysfunction (~30% with elevated AST alone, ~50% with elevated AST and bilirubin). Reduce dose to 1/2 (bilirubin 1.2-3 mg/dL or AST 2-4x ULN) or 1/4 (bilirubin >3 mg/dL or AST >4x ULN). Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C or bilirubin >5 mg/dL).

major: Cardiotoxic agents (e.g., trastuzumab - persists up to 7 months; avoid anthracyclines for up to 7 months after; calcium channel blockers) - additive cardiotoxicity
Cimetidine - increases epirubicin exposure; discontinue cimetidine during treatment
Live or live-attenuated vaccines - risk of serious/fatal infection; avoid
moderate: Paclitaxel - increases systemic exposure of epirubicin and metabolites
Docetaxel - increases exposure of epirubicin metabolites
Other cytotoxic drugs - additive hematologic and GI toxicity
Radiation therapy - potentiation of toxicity and radiation recall
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; avoid additional hepatotoxic exposures.
interactions.diagnostics: Urine may appear red for 1-2 days after administration (harmless).

emergency: Acute left ventricular failure / CHF (chest pain, dyspnea, dizziness)

monitoring: LVEF at baseline and regularly during and after treatment; ECG at baseline
CBC with differential and platelets before each cycle (WBC nadir ~10-14 days)
Serum total bilirubin and AST before and during therapy
Serum creatinine before and during therapy
Uric acid, potassium, calcium, phosphate after initial treatment (tumor lysis)
Cumulative epirubicin dose (generally avoid exceeding 900 mg/m2)
Infusion site for signs of extravasation
counsel: There is a risk of irreversible heart muscle damage; immediately report chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, or lightheadedness
Report fever or signs of infection promptly (low blood counts)
Report any pain, burning, or swelling at the injection site during or after infusion
Urine may turn red for 1-2 days after a dose - this is harmless
There is an increased long-term risk of treatment-related leukemia
May cause irreversible amenorrhea or premature menopause and may impair fertility; use effective contraception as directed
pk: Immediate (IV cytotoxic effect); marrow nadir ~10-14 days
Cmax at end of 6-10 min infusion (~5.7-9.3 mcg/mL at 60-150 mg/m2)
Terminal (gamma) ~31-35 hours; triphasic decline (~3 min, ~2.5 h, ~33 h)
Refrigerate 2-8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze; protect from light; use within 24 h after removal from refrigeration
pearls: BOXED WARNING: cardiotoxicity, secondary AML/MDS, extravasation/necrosis, and severe myelosuppression
Cumulative-dose cardiomyopathy risk rises from 0.9% at 550 mg/m2 to 3.3% at 900 mg/m2; generally avoid exceeding 900 mg/m2
Powerful vesicant - treat extravasation as an emergency (ice, dexrazoxane within 6 h)
Reduce dose for hepatic impairment; contraindicated if severe (Child-Pugh C or bilirubin >5 mg/dL)
Avoid combining with other cardiotoxic agents; wait up to 7 months after trastuzumab when possible
Must be administered by a clinician experienced in cytotoxic chemotherapy
missed: Not self-administered. Epirubicin is given on a scheduled cycle by oncology staff; a delayed cycle is rescheduled by the treating team based on counts and toxicity recovery (platelets >=100,000/mm3, ANC >=1500/mm3, nonhematologic toxicity <= Grade 1).
overdose: No known antidote. Acute high-dose exposure causes severe myelosuppression (bone marrow aplasia within ~10-14 days), grade 4 mucositis, GI bleeding, and may be fatal (e.g., multiorgan failure reported). Delayed CHF can occur months later. Provide supportive care: antibiotics, blood/platelet transfusions, colony-stimulating factors, and intensive care; observe long-term for CHF.
